note: The Dallas County results report for the May 8, 2010 joint election lists one Garland city contest, Garland District 05. It lists no Garland mayoral contest. The Dallas County 2013 entity listing shows the Garland mayor term as 2 years, ending 2015, and the City of Garland elections page names the mayor as next elected on May 1, 2027, so Garland elects its mayor in odd-numbered years.

Garland elects its mayor in odd years on a two-year term, so a mayoral seat was due in 2011. The official City of Garland newsletter Garland City Press, June 2011 (source_url, 8 pages, text extracted and read), says Mayor Ronald E. Jones ran unopposed in the May municipal election and began his third and final term, and that he was sworn in at a special meeting on May 23. The Dallas County report for the May 14, 2011 joint election lists only Garland District 06 and no mayoral contest. These sources show that the mayor had no opponent. They do not show whether the city cancelled the election and declared the candidate elected, or held a ballot, and they give no election date. No cancellation order, council canvass or other election-authority document for 2011 was found. Second pass: the Brave searches through mac2 for a 2011 order, council minutes or cancellation notice returned only later-year pages and Ballotpedia. The Internet Archive CDX queries for garlandtx.gov/gov/cd/secretary timed out. WebFetch of www.garlandtx.gov/gov/cd/secretary/elections.asp returned HTTP 500. WebSearch was unavailable because its budget was used. The earlier no_election status is withdrawn, because the mayoral seat was filled by an unopposed candidacy in 2011 and a newsletter is not an election-authority record. The year is not recorded as complete, because there is no official document or date for the uncontested election. No results row is written for the same reason. A reader with the City Secretary's 2011 canvass or cancellation ordinance can set the year to complete with Ronald E. Jones as sole winner. The 2013 Garland City Press (Item 346) states that Douglas Athas replaced Jones after term limits, which is consistent with the odd-year cycle. The same unopposed treatment applies to 2015, where the Dallas County entity listing states the city cancelled its mayoral election.
